headline: US and Denmark strike a deal on Greenland's security
summary: Trump announced it Friday on Truth Social, saying it gives the US "permanent control over security" in Greenland at no cost. Denmark's prime minister says it recognizes the Kingdom's sovereignty and Greenlanders' right to self-determination. It will be signed at the UN next week, after months of Trump threats to take the island.
cover_answer: No. Denmark keeps it. The US gets to run its security.
table_question: Is a deal fair if one side threatened to just take it?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Greenland is a giant icy island that belongs to Denmark, and the president wanted it for America. Instead the two countries made a deal: Denmark keeps it, and America helps guard it. Like a neighbor who watches your yard but doesn't move in. The grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Wanting something, being told no, and settling on a share is a story every five-year-old has lived.

8-12.script: For months Trump said the US should take Greenland, part of Denmark. Denmark said it is not for sale. Friday they announced a deal: Denmark keeps Greenland, the US builds a bigger military presence and gets a veto on rival bases. A lease, not a sale.
8-12.why: Threat, refusal, compromise is a chain they can follow.

13-17.script: Is Greenland ours now? No. Denmark keeps it, and Greenlanders keep the right to self-determination. Trump says the US gets "permanent control over security" and a big military presence. Partnership, or a takeover with paperwork?
13-17.why: Teens can weigh one deal described from two capitals.

5-7.a: It sits in a spot that's useful for defense, and it has valuable minerals in the ground. Denmark said it was not for sale.

8-12.q: So who's in charge of Greenland?
8-12.a: Denmark, and Greenland's own people. Trump says the US gets "permanent control over security." Details come at the signing.
Its prime minister says it strengthens Arctic security and recognizes Danish sovereignty. She didn't address Trump's claims.

13-17.a: No. Denmark keeps sovereignty. Trump says the US gets "permanent control over security" and a big military presence.

13-17.q: Why would Denmark agree after being threatened?
13-17.a: Its PM says it strengthens Arctic security and recognizes Danish sovereignty. The US already had access under a 1951 deal.
